questions.concept: Origin and evolution of Universe Solar system
questions.question: Minal wrote an essay on the largest moon of Saturn. Which among the following moons is it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Titan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Titan:-**

 
 
• **It is the second-largest moon in the Solar System, after Jupiter's moon Ganymede. **
 
• It is also the only known moon in the Solar System to have a dense atmosphere, and the only known world besides Earth on which clear evidence of stable bodies of surface liquid has been found.
 
• **Titan's atmosphere is primarily made of nitrogen, with a small fraction of methane. **
 
• The dense atmosphere frequently produces bright white convective clouds, especially over the south pole region. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carme:-**

 
 
• **It is a retrograde irregular satellite of Jupiter. **
 
• It was discovered by Seth Barnes Nicholson at Mount Wilson Observatory in California in July 1938.
 
• It is named after the mythological Carme, mother by Zeus of Britomartis, a Cretan goddess.
 
 
 
• **Atlas:-**
 
 
• **It is a small inner moon of Saturn. **
 
• It was discovered in 1980 by Richard Terrile from Voyager photos and was designated S/1980 S 28. 
 
 
 
• **Europa:-**
 
 
• **It is one of the most intriguing moons in the Solar System. **
 
• It is the sixth-largest moon in the Solar System and the fourth-largest of Jupiter's moons.
 
• Europa is slightly smaller than Earth's Moon, but it is more massive than all known moons in the Solar System smaller than itself combined.

questions.question: Which of the following is a dwarf planet of our solar system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Makemake.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Makemake is the 3rd largest dwarf planet__ in the solar system.
 
• It is the __2nd farthest dwarf planet__ from the Sun.
 
• Makemake was discovered by scientists in the year 2005 and was recognized as a dwarf planet by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in July 2008. 
 
• __Examples of Dwarf planets__: Eris, Pluto, and Haumea.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Callisto** is the third largest satellite in the solar system and is almost the size of Mercury. 
 
• Ganymede is a satellite of Jupiter and the largest satellite in our solar system.
 
 
• It is larger than Mercury and Pluto, and three-quarters the size of Mars.
 
 
 
• **Europa** is the smallest moon of Jupiter.

questions.question: Cosmic snowballs of frozen gases, rock and dust that orbit the Sun are known as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Comets.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Comets:-**

 
 
• These are **cosmic snowballs** of **frozen gases, rock, and dust** that orbit the Sun.
 
• They have a **coma**, a fuzzy atmosphere of gas and dust that surrounds the nucleus, and a **tail** that points away from the Sun.
 
• Comets are believed to be remnants from the **formation of the Solar System.**
 
• They can have** highly elliptical orbits **and can take hundreds or thousands of years to complete one orbit around the Sun.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meteors:-**

 
 
• These are small rocks or debris that** burn up** upon entering Earth's atmosphere, while **meteorites **are any **surviving pieces** that reach the ground.
 
 
 
• **Stars:-**
 
 
• These are massive, luminous spheres of **plasma** held together by **gravity.**
 
 
 
• **Meteorites**:-
 
 
• These are pieces of rock or metal that have fallen to Earth from space.
 
• They are the only physical evidence we have of what exists beyond our planet, and they can provide valuable insights into the formation and evolution of the solar system.

questions.question: Which of the following celestial bodies has a natural satellite named ‘Charon’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pluto**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pluto **____**has a natural satellite named ‘Charon’**__.

 __
 
• **Charon also known as Pluto I** is the largest of the five known natural satellites of the dwarf planet Pluto.
 
• It has a mean radius of 606 km.
 
• **Charon is the sixth-largest known trans-Neptunian object** after Pluto, Eris, Haumea, Makemake, and Gonggong.
 
• It was discovered in **1978 **at the United States Naval Observatory in Washington, D.C., using photographic plates taken at the United States Naval Observatory Flagstaff Station (NOFS).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mars **is the fourth planet from the Sun and the second-smallest planet in the Solar System, being larger than only Mercury.

 
 
• In English, Mars carries the name of the Roman god of war and is often referred to as the "**Red Planet**". 
 
 
 
• **Saturn** is the sixth planet from the Sun and the second-largest in the Solar System, after Jupiter. It is a gas giant with an average radius of about nine and a half times that of Earth.
 
 
• It only has **one-eighth** the average density of Earth; however, with its larger volume, Saturn is over **95 times** more massive.
 
 
 
• **Haumea** is a dwarf planet located beyond Neptune's orbit.
 
 
• It was discovered in **2004 **by a team headed by Mike Brown of Caltech at the Palomar Observatory in the United States and disputably also in 2005.

questions.question: The average separation between the sun and the earth in terms of light years is 8.311 minutes. Here, minutes indicate:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**distance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Light travels at a speed of approximately **299,792 kilometers per second** in a vacuum.
 
• The average distance between the Earth and the Sun is about **149.6 million kilometers**, which light covers in approximately **8.311 minutes**.
 
• When we mention "minutes" in this context, we are referring to **the time it takes for light to travel a certain distance**.
 
• This measurement is used to represent **distance in terms of the time taken by light to traverse it**, a common practice in astronomy.
 
• Thus, the term "minutes" in this context symbolizes **distance, not time.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Light Year:**

 
 
• A light year is the distance that light travels in one year in a vacuum.
 
• It is approximately **9.46 trillion kilometers** or **5.88 trillion miles**.
 
• It is a unit used to measure astronomical distances between celestial objects.
 
 
 
• **Astronomical Unit (AU):**
 
 
• The Astronomical Unit is the average distance between the Earth and the Sun.
 
• 1 AU is approximately **149.6 million kilometers**.
 
• It is commonly used to describe distances within our solar system.
 
 
 
• **Speed of Light:**
 
 
• The speed of light is a universal constant, denoted by "c," with a value of approximately **299,792 kilometers per second**.
 
• It is the fastest speed at which information or matter can travel.
 
 
 
• **Time and Distance Relationship in Astronomy:**
 
 
• In astronomy, distances are often expressed in terms of the time light takes to travel (e.g., light-years, light-minutes).
 
• This method makes it easier to comprehend vast distances in the universe.

• Meteors are bits of rock and ice that are ejected from comets as they manoeuvre around their orbits around the sun. 
 
• Meteor showers are witnessed when Earth passes through the trail of debris left behind by a comet or an asteroid.
 
• When a meteor reaches the Earth, it is called a meteorite and a series of meteorites, when encountered at once, is termed a meteor shower. 
 
• As meteors fall towards the Earth, the resistance makes the space rocks extremely hot and, as meteorites pass through the atmosphere, they leave behind streaks of glowing gas that are visible to the observers and not the rock itself

questions.question: The Kuiper Belt is a ring of icy rocks & dust bodies just outside the orbit of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neptune.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kuiper Belt **is a region in the **outer solar system **beyond the orbit of **Neptune, **consisting of small icy objects like **comets and dwarf planets.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saturn **is located in the** inner solar system**, between Jupiter and Uranus, and does not have any significant icy asteroid belt beyond its orbit.
 
• **Venus** is an inner planet,** closer to the Sun than Earth,** and has no known asteroid belt or Kuiper Belt objects in its vicinity.
 
• **Jupiter** is the **largest planet in the solar system** and has its own set of **Trojan asteroids** in its orbit, but it is not located beyond Neptune where the Kuiper Belt exists.
 
• **Neptune** is the eighth planet from the Sun and is known to have a **well-defined Kuiper Belt region** that extends from about **30 AU to 50 AU** from the Sun.

questions.concept: Origin and evolution of Universe Solar system
questions.question: Which planet in the solar system is considered as Earth’s twin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Venus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Venus as the twin of the earth:__
 
• Venus is sometimes called Earth's twin because Venus and Earth are almost the same size, have about the same mass (they weigh about the same), and have a very similar composition (are made of the same material).
 
• They are also neighbouring planets.
 
• However, Venus and Earth are also very different.
 
• Venus has an atmosphere that is about 100 times thicker than Earth's and has surface temperatures that are extremely hot.
 
• Venus does not have life or water oceans like Earth does.
 
• Venus also rotates backwards compared to Earth and the other planets.

*Hence, Venus is considered as ‘Earth’s-twin’ because its size and shape are very much similar to that of the earth.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

__
 
• 
 
**M**y **V**ery **E**xcited **M**other **J**ust **S**erved **U**s **N**achos

 

M → Mercury, V → Venus, E → Earth, M → Mars, J → Jupiter, S → Saturn, U → Uranus, N → Neptune

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The Solar System contains 8 planets:

 
 

 Inner or Terrestrial planets

 
 
 
 
 
 
• Mercury
 
• Venus
 
• Earth
 
• Mars
 
 
 
 

 
 Outer Planets or Jovian planets

 
 
 
 
 
 
• Jupiter
 
• Saturn
 
• Uranus
 
• Neptune
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd35273a568fcc91584ab0c4c1d6b40046dcf73b04a0c1577fdee83407159359.png]

questions.concept: Origin and evolution of Universe Solar system
questions.question: Which among the following planets is also known as Earth's twin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Venus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Venus: 

 
 
• Venus is Earth's twin in size.
 
• Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system.
 
• It is the brightest planet in the Solar System.
 
• It is also sometimes referred to as the sister planet to Earth, due to their near similarity of size and mass.
 
• Venus is referred to as the “morning star” and “evening star”.
 
• It is the second planet from the Sun.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neptune**

 
 
• It is a Bluish-Greenish Planet.
 
• Neptune is the fourth-largest planet in diameter.
 
• In terms of mass, it is 17 times the mass of Earth.
 
• It takes 160 years approximately to orbit around the sun.
 
• Its atmosphere comprises hydrogen and helium.
 
• The absorption of red light by the atmosphere due to the trace amount of Methane gives this planet a greenish-blue to hue colour. 
 
 
 
• Jupiter:
 
 
• Jupiter is the planet, **orange **in color with white bands on it.
 
• Jupiter is the** largest planet **in the **Solar System**.
 
• Jupiter's atmosphere is mostly made up of hydrogen (**H2**) and helium (**He**).
 
 
 
• Saturn:
 
 
• Saturn is known most for its **rings**.
 
• It is the **second-largest** planet in our solar system.
 
• Saturn's atmosphere is also mostly made up of hydrogen (**H2**) and helium (**He**).
